written_before_results: Expectations come from domain reasoning about Dutch courts, not from output.

text_fields.summary: Court-written case summary. Often names the legal area, so it can leak the label.
text_fields.ruling_excerpt: First 2,500 characters of the ruling. Parties and headers dominate; leaks less.

procedure.why: Procedure type (appeal, cassation, injunction) changes the register.

court_type.why: Hoge Raad, Raad van State and district courts write differently and hear different matters.

court.why: Individual courts specialise a little; place names appear in texts.

year.why: Topics drift slowly; only some laws and events are dated.

summary_words.why: Text length itself. Should not outrank real structure once length is controlled.

ruling_words.why: Full ruling length, correlated with the excerpt only indirectly.

ecli_sequence.why: Running number within court and year; may proxy court size. Reported, not scored.

scored_as.primary: every strong column outranks every null control
scored_as.secondary: strong and moderate columns versus null controls (AUC)
scored_as.confound: length columns rank below every strong column
